text: Maya Patel: FYI the docs CI is failing with a ton of broken fragment errors after the recent headings rename in the runtime guide. build log shows 'Broken fragment: #using-the-runtime' and similar for several pages. Jordan Lee: ugh. Is it the new slugify behavior or a migration mismatch from the old anchors? Maya Patel: looks like slug clashes + some headings that include inline code backticks. mkdocs' slugify normalized them differently than our older script. Samir Khan: can you paste an example? Maya Patel: sure — snippet from mkdocs linkcheck: ``Broken fragment: /guides/runtime/#using-the-runtime``; original heading was "Using the runtime (v2)" and we added ` using the runtime` in code block earlier which changed the slug. Priya Nair: I hit this locally too. Running `mkdocs build` with the current plugin set reproduces it. I think mkdocs-material's slugify changed in the last upgrade. Alex Morris: quick mitigation: we can add explicit anchors where slugs changed. e.g. in markdown add "" above the heading or add a manual slug: `### Using the runtime {#using-the-runtime}` Jordan Lee: prefer manual slug fallback in the few affected pages rather than pinning the plugin. Do we have a list of pages? Maya Patel: I grepped the logs and got a short list: `/guides/runtime/`, `/guides/deploy/`, `/api/versions/` — I'll attach the failing lines to the PR. docs-bot: linkcheck job failed for commit 3f9a2b1 — https://ci.internal.redwood/links/1207 Samir Khan: I'll open a small docs PR that adds manual slugs for the runtime and deploy pages. Want to include a short note in the PR description about why (slugify change). Priya Nair: When you do that, add a line to the migration guide (docs/migration/slugs.md) so authors know to use `{#manual-slug}` for headings that include inline code or parentheses. Alex Morris: Also check our mkdocs config. We had `use_directory_urls: true` and a custom plugin for anchor normalization. Maybe the plugin needs tweaking. If we can update the plugin to mirror the old behavior, that's another route. Jordan Lee: For now let's do manual slugs + a quick CI patch to whitelist the three pages so staging doesn't block deploy. Maya Patel: plan: Samir opens PR with manual slugs + update migration note. I will add the failing log lines to the PR. Priya, can you QA the branch locally? Priya Nair: Yup, will run `mkdocs serve` and `mkdocs build` + `mkdocs linkcheck` locally and confirm. Samir Khan: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 — includes manual slugs and a comment in migration guide. Marking @Priya for QA. Priya Nair: Reviewing now. Quick aside: one of the pages still 404s because it has an inline emoji in the heading (shock). We should add a small note in the style guide about avoiding emoji in headings or normalizing them. Maya Patel: noted — add to the migration note. Alex Morris: Once PR merges, we should run a full linkcheck job on staging. I'll queue a manual run. docs-bot: manual linkcheck queued by Alex Morris — job 1240 Jordan Lee: Post-merge step: run a site diff (html output) to ensure no TOC changes beyond slugs. We want minimal churn. Samir Khan: Updated PR with a brief test plan and the grep results. Leaving one TODO for Alex to start the staging linkcheck after merge. Maya Patel: thanks all — seems small and surgical. If staging passes, I'll backport the manual slugs to the stable branch for the imminent release. Priya Nair: LGTM after local linkcheck passes. Alex Morris: I'll run staging linkcheck and report back here. docs-bot: linkcheck job 1240 completed — 0 broken fragments on staging Alex Morris: staging linkcheck green. merging PR in 5. Samir Khan: merged and bumped patch version on docs site config. Maya Patel: merging note: filed a tiny follow-up issue to audit headings that contain inline code/emoji and add linter rule. Issue #456. Jordan Lee: nice work everyone. :tada:
